findings.text: the Gate paragraph asserts that 'the wider five-file gate (180 tests, adding test_skill_contracts.py, test_ledger.py and test_a_pick_sees_each_review_dimension.py) adds no failure against the base revision 49b9973b4' with a single named failure, but no log or stream record shows that gate completing: the run's own manifest.md:11 records only the four-file head gate (tests/test_skill_contracts.py, tests/test_crew_help_names_*.py, tests/test_a_corrected_review_row_reads_as_unreviewed.py, tests/test_cited_commands_exist.py), and the 180 figure is the worker's arithmetic projection (7+5+67+97+4) rather than an observed summary. The done-when names tests/test_ledger.py and tests/test_a_pick_sees_each_review_dimension.py -- the existing tests that cover ledger.review_scores and the picker review dimension this change edits -- and neither was run in the recorded gate, so the node's evidence claims a result it never measured.

the after_suite and baseline_suite 'command' fields read 'uv run pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q ...' while the cited head-gate.log and base-arm.log headers record 'PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -rA ...', so the recorded gate command does not match the log it cites.

the private _node_head_suffix is now a byte-for-byte duplicate of the new package owner reckon/crew/repair.py:331 round_node_head_suffix; the census script should import the repair module's inverse of round_node_id rather than keep a second copy of the head-suffix grammar, so the two cannot drift.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from 49b9973b4 to bd3cd5c35; five commits touch 11 files -- review_block in reckon/ledger.py, round_node_head_suffix in reckon/crew/repair.py, the verb in reckon/crew_run_commands.py, four reader routings, the new test file, the skill and contract classification, and the landing fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when's five-file gate names tests/test_ledger.py and tests/test_a_pick_sees_each_review_dimension.py; the recorded head gate (head-gate.log) runs four files omitting both, and the landing fragment claims a 180-test five-file result no log records (see FINDING).
item_verdicts.goal_fidelity: the goal is a supersede-review verb that appends a review_correction and routes every reader of a row's review through one accessor; reckon/crew_run_commands.py:806 defines supersede_run_review and reckon/ledger.py:3675 defines review_block, both present only at the head and used by the four named readers.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the four-file head gate green (81 passed, EXIT=0) at bd3cd5c35, the base arm at 49b9973b4 (2 failed, 72 passed), the negative control, and the landing line; its after_suite/baseline_suite commands do not match the logs they cite.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff touches the declared paths plus tests/test_skill_contracts.py and skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md; prompt.txt:69-80 does not grant those two, but the resume brief (resume-1-advice.txt) explicitly widens the fence to include them, so the writes are sanctioned.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_corrected_review_row_reads_as_unreviewed.py:247-254 reddens if any reader re-reads the stale block (review_block would return the block, picker_reviews would be [0.75]) and the negative-control base arm shows all 7 cases failing by id at 49b9973b4, so each case names the code change that would break it.
justifications.evidence: head-gate.log records 81 passed, EXIT=0 at bd3cd5c35 and negative-control-base-arm.log records the 7 new cases failing by id at 49b9973b4, but tests/test_ledger.py and tests/test_a_pick_sees_each_review_dimension.py -- named in the done-when -- were run by no recorded gate (see FINDING at the fragment).
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/repair.py:331 and reckon/ledger.py:3675 follow the surrounding docstring-and-structure idiom and introduce no plan, ticket or version identifier; the new verb is now carried into the skills/reckon-build SKILL.md contract beside its siblings.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew_run_commands.py:806 supersede_run_review appends review_correction {time, reason, dispatched_head, recorded_head, superseded_field} without rewriting the recorded fields, and reckon/ledger.py:3686 review_block returns None for a corrected row so it drops out of totals and medians as the goal states.
justifications.reuse: review_block is defined on the row owner (reckon/ledger.py:3675) and the four readers call it rather than reading row['review']; round_node_head_suffix sits beside round_node_source (reckon/crew/repair.py:312) as the inverse of round_node_id, and the verb reuses _review_record_subject, carried_revision_pair, same_revision and _commit_landing_writes -- but it duplicates the census script's already-existing _node_head_suffix (see follow-on FINDING).
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff 49b9973b4..bd3cd5c35 is inside the SCOPE fence in prompt.txt:69-80 once the resume-1-advice.txt widening of skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md and tests/test_skill_contracts.py is honoured; reckon/cli.py was declared and left unchanged.
